mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 4% over the prior month reduces the discount rate applied to future corporate earnings, lowering the present value of expected cash flows and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns in the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by 0.5 percentage points over the past month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite the FEDFUNDS increase, or the effect size is statistically insignificant in a 5-year backtest.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 20,000 jobs while UNRATE falls by 0.5 percentage points within the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite the labor indicators moving in the predicted direction, or the effect is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) relative to GDP (GDPC1) indicates excess demand in the economy, prompting central banks to keep rates steady and encouraging investors to price in higher future earnings, which elevates S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL growth rate exceeds GDP growth rate by 2 percentage points in the current quarter
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns underperform a baseline model that uses only lagged SPX returns, t-test p > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) over three consecutive months suggests weakening supply-side constraints, reducing production costs and improving profit margins, which supports higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative or the effect is not detectable in a rolling window regression.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate remains persistently below 2% during a period of declining inflation (CPIAUCSL), it signals accommodative policy that lowers real interest rates, encouraging risk-taking and pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases for two consecutive months while FEDFUNDS stays below 2%
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are flat or negative despite the policy regime.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) without a corresponding rise in job openings (PAYEMS) indicates a tight labor market, raising wage growth expectations and pushing S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls by 0.3 percentage points while PAYEMS increases by less than 10,000 jobs
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative or the effect is absent in a difference-in-differences test.

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a post-crisis expansion characterized by rising consumer confidence (indirect proxy via HOUST) and stable inflation (CPIAUCSL) predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days, regardless of interest rate path.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in all regimes where the indicators confirm expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the federal funds rate above 5% triggers a sharp repricing of risk assets as investors anticipate higher future discount rates, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by 1 percentage point in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from the pre-move baseline in a two-tailed test.
